A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same mental-rotation model and VR study. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original VR experiments with 19 participants, computational model evaluations, and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original human and model experiments and adds a trial-level analysis of human–human and human–model error consistency.

M1.justification: The equivariant renderer, symbolic encoder–decoder, and five-class decision MLP remain unchanged, including their training objectives and recurrent rotation procedure. Material moved into Appendix E documents the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same VR population, Shepard–Metzler objects, match/mirror tasks, rotation conditions, and Ganis–Kievit data analysis. The new 550-trial error comparison remains within existing task and population coverage.

E2.justification: The ResNet-18/34/50, ViT-B-16, and SL-ViT Siamese baselines and existing component ablations are retained. Their participation is unchanged in v1 Figure 21 versus v2 Figure 17 and Section 5.1; newly cited models are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 Appendix E.3 adds an evaluation of correctness agreement over 550 Action-setup trials using error consistency based on Cohen's kappa. Existing training budgets, object splits, participant exclusions, and main evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds an error analysis asking whether human cohorts and the model make the same mistakes. Figure 11 also newly reports similar reaction-time variability within individual subjects, although those results are not plotted. Existing ablations and action/reaction-time analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix E.3 adds chance-corrected agreement estimation, explicitly calculating observed correctness overlap and expected overlap from observer accuracies. Neither version supplies repeated-training-run counts, seeds, or uncertainty intervals for these comparisons.

E6.justification: v2 adds human–human error consistency of 0.163 and model–human values of 0.01 and 0.08. On the 550-trial comparison, cohort accuracies are 96.18% and 94.73%, and model accuracy is 96.18%. These are additional results, not an improvement over the unchanged 96.13% main-test accuracy; existing baseline and ablation scores are retained.

T1.justification: The quadrant invariance/equivariance formalism and training and inference equations are retained, with relocation into Appendices D and E. The added kappa equation states the standard agreement metric used for evaluation; it introduces no new theoretical result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the claims of a mechanistic neural model combining spatial and symbolic representations to explain human mental-rotation behavior. Explicitly listing partial reaction-time explanation in v2's Discussion restates a claim already developed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly concludes that the model does not capture humans' errors despite similar accuracy. Its Figure 11 caption also argues that reaction-time variability cannot be explained solely by different slopes across individuals. Existing biological-plausibility, generalization, and reaction-time limitations remain, partly relocated.

D1.justification: v1 states that experimental data will be released upon publication; v2 states that code and experimental data are available through the project repository. This changes the reported access information. Architecture, hardware, optimization, rendering, and split details are otherwise largely retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the error analysis and cognitive discussion, acknowledges Bonnen et al. (2026), including its reaction-time relationship, and broadens the JEPA comparison to latent equivariant operators. These refine the existing positioning without redefining the contribution.

P1.justification: The main narrative is substantially condensed and reorganized. Literature and discussion passages move into new Appendices A and B, while detailed model equations, baseline descriptions, and behavioral analyses are consolidated in Appendix E. Many accompanying paragraphs and transitions are rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main layout, adds an illustrated ablation-summary table, merges behavioral and architecture figures, and redraws action distributions as normalized comparisons. The human-results table moves to the appendix, duplicate displays are consolidated, and the action-counting illustration is revised.

improvement.justification: Relative to v1's aggregate behavioral comparisons, v2's error-consistency analysis more clearly exposes limits of human–model agreement. Reported data availability and consolidated comparison displays also improve transparency and readability. These are useful but limited gains: the method and principal results remain unchanged, and the new agreement estimates lack uncertainty quantification.
